evals.prompt: We're missing an ops-friendly liveness probe on the proxy itself. Add a /healthz endpoint to go-reverse-flow: it should return 200 with a tiny JSON body when at least one backend in the pool is healthy, and 503 when none are. Wire it on the mux in cmd/proxy, keep it out of the proxied chain, cover it with tests, and make sure the usual gates pass.
evals.expected_output: A healthz endpoint wired in cmd/proxy/main.go using health.Checker state (not a new mechanism), tests alongside the change in the right package, stdlib-only code in repo idioms, gate commands run, and no unrelated files touched.
expectations: GET /healthz returns 200 with a JSON body when at least one backend is healthy and 503 when none are
The endpoint is mounted on the mux in cmd/proxy/main.go, outside the proxied middleware chain
The endpoint reuses the existing health checker state - no new probing mechanism
Ships new tests covering the verdict contract
Ran the verification gate (vet/test/build) and reported results honestly, including the -race/cgo limitation
Lands as a single atomic Conventional Commit containing only the endpoint slice

evals.prompt: Before I trust SmoothWeighted in prod: review internal/balancer/smooth.go for concurrency safety under heavy request load plus health demotions shrinking the candidate list at the same time. Hunt for data races and fairness bugs. If you find a real bug, fix it with a regression test; otherwise report findings and don't touch the code.
evals.expected_output: A review report grounded in the actual file: mutex-guarded URL-keyed state, weight-1 default for unknown candidates after demotions, Pick's map+current bookkeeping all covered by the single mutex, plus reference to the existing race tests. Either a justified no-bug report or a minimal fix with test. No speculative refactors.
expectations: Reports a race-safety verdict for smooth.go with file:line evidence of lock coverage
Analyzes fairness under demotions (frozen currents / conservation invariant)
Backs the analysis with empirical or closed-form verification, not bare assertion
Runs vet/test/build and handles the missing -race constraint honestly
Makes no code changes given no real bug was found (respects the review-only bar)

evals.prompt: Do a security pass over internal/cache (the TTL response cache middleware). I care about: cache poisoning, responses leaking between clients, and memory-exhaustion vectors. List findings with severity; only write code if you find an actual exploitable bug, and otherwise leave the carefully chosen behavior alone.
evals.expected_output: Findings report referencing the real eligibility rules: Set-Cookie exclusion, no-store handling, Accept-Encoding bypass of the single-key scheme, 1 MiB + Content-Length match bound, X-Cache-Bypass escape hatch, RWMutex-guarded items map. Exploitability framed honestly against the buffered-serve path. No drive-by behavior changes.
expectations: Identifies Range/206 partial-content storage under the shared key as a cache-poisoning vector
Identifies the Authorization/Cookie keying gap enabling cross-client response leaks
Distinguishes documented accepted limitations from actual exploitable bugs
Fixes actual exploitable bugs with regression tests in atomic fix commits (task bar: code only for real exploitable bugs)
Runs the verification gate and reports results honestly
Follows reproduce-then-fix discipline (PoC or test-first evidence) when fixing vulnerabilities
